Traders reported that quotations for imported cathode fell slightly in the past two weeks. Some of the most recent quotations were in the range of $80-100/t, while premiums for SXEW cathode were being quoted at $80-90/t. As a result of the LME copper price surging, the arbitrage window between SHFE and LME closed since opening May. Market insiders reported that seaborne cathode availability is down as a result of increased buying activity for imported cathode in May and June. Nonetheless, as the cyclically weak Q3 approaches and import loss widens, demand for cathode is falling. Import loss widened to around RMB2,000/t compared to RMB1,000/t two weeks ago. According to preliminary data from Chinese customs, China imported 280,009t of unwrought copper and copper semis in June, up 9.9% m-o-m. We believe that this was in response to the arbitrage turning positive in May and June, which reflected market anticipation. Moreover, traders expect that cathode imports in July will continue to rally as shipments due to arbitrage trade usually take two weeks to one month to arrive. We predict that spot premiums will face downward pressure in the coming weeks if the LME copper price remains at its current level. Furthermore, domestic consumers need time to consume bonded materials which saw a significant decline of around 225,000t in May and June. China produced 477,000t of cathode in June, up 8.6% m-o-m and 12.0% y-o-y based on NBS data. # **High speed railway developments will boost copper demand** It was reported that the railway sector will be one of the fastest growing end-use sectors for copper in the next decade. According to the Ministry of Railways, China’s investment into railways will amount to RMB2.8T in the next five years, compared to RMB2.2T in the past five years. The total mileage of China's railway operations is expected to rise from the current 91,000km to 120,000km by 2015. The mileage of high-speed railway alone will rise from 8,358km in 2010 to 16,000km by 2015. The electrification rate will increase to 60%, compared to 46% in 2010. Wires and cables used for railway and train construction are classified as rolling stock cables. The major types within this category include communication cables, power/signalling cables and other components, such as winding wires and strips that wind around traction motors and transformers. Moreover, pantographs (a device on the roofs of electric trains and locomotives that picks up the electr

ic current from overhead wires) and track cables are installed beside the track or above the train for electrification purposes. At present, the most commonly used overhead conductor for high–speed railway lines is copper alloy wire, which contain over 90% copper. Other elements such as silver, tin and magnesium are added for strength. Shenyang Beiheng Copper is one of major local producers that manufacture the bare copper alloy wire for high-speed trains, with annual output of nearly 30,000t. Ganzhou Jiangwu-La Farga HighSpeed Railway Copper Materials, who produce copper and alloy products for the railway industry, completed their phase one 40,000t/y trial production in March. There have also been reports of Chalco Kunming Copper planning to bring on capacity to produce overhead conductors for high-speed railway lines by the end of 2011. 

# **MIIT issued list of old technology to be phased out** 

On 11<sup>th</sup> July, China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) announced the list for the elimination of outdated production capacity enterprises, under a strategy to improve energy efficiency, conserve resources and curb pollution. The list of outdated production capacity enterprises was also published on local government websites. According to the announcement, the Chinese Government plans to eliminate 425,300t/y of outdated copper smelting capacity by the end of 2011. Other nonferrous metals which will be affected include 618,600t/y of aluminium refining capacity, 338,300t/y of zinc smelting capacity and 660,900t/y of lead smelting capacity. The list of outdated copper smelting capacity enterprises set specific reduction targets regionally, including196,900t/y in Jiangxi, 95,200t/y in Henan, 50,000t/y in Shanxi, 32,000t/y in Yunnan, 29,000t/y in Hunan, 11,000t/y in Xinjiang, 10,000t/y in Gansu and 1,200t/y in Chongqing. 

Market insiders are concerned about the difference between two MIIT announcements. In May, MIIT announced that the Chinese Government plans to eliminate 291,000t/y of outdated copper smelting capacity by the end of 2011. Last time, only Yunnan, Hunan and Chongqing published figures on the amount of outdated copper smelting capacity that they each expect to eliminate. The capacity identified by these three provinces was the same after both announcements. We therefore believe that the latest

The LME 3-month copper price surged to $9,738/t on 8th July, driven by strong U.S. economic data, the strike at Codelco and strong demand expectations. In response, the SHFE 3-month copper price rose to above RMB70,000/t, climbing to RMB72,460/t on Wednesday, the highest level since mid-April 2011. We noticed that the Shanghai physical market moved into a discount when copper price rose. At the same time, the price difference between the SHFE cash month and the 3-month moved into contango from the beginning of July. On the one hand, this indicates that demand became subdued as a result of the weak Q3 approaching as well as buying activity being constrained by higher copper prices. On the other hand, we believe that market sentiment has changed, with market insiders’ copper price expectations becoming more positive. We believe that cathode demand will become weak in July and August, however not by much. We were told by some large wire and cable manufacturers that they are currently operating at full capacity and that their new orders forecast remains optimistic. This is the result of China’s infrastructure projects, which are driven by a RMB4T stimulus package, entering the wire and cable installation stage. We understand that the substantial support for copper prices is currently driven by China’s low cathode inventories, including Shanghai bonded materials, SHFE stocks and consumer stocks. However, this does not mean China will restock immediately. The approaching weak Q3 will have a negative impact on cathode consumption, although probably to a limited degree. At the same time, the domestic market needs time to consume the significant bonded warehouse inventories released over the past two months. With the arbitrage window closed, imports are unlikely to rally, leaving the market in deficit in Q3 and prices supported at a high level. However, we believe that it is unlikely for the copper price to continue its surge in the coming two months due to the uncertainty in financial markets.
